To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the distinction between intrinsic and extrinsic motivations is a critical one for understanding how people behave, (2) the distinction between the two types of motivations has been over-simplified, and (3) the distinction between autonomous and controlled extrinsic motivations is important for understanding the effects of extrinsic rewards on intrinsic motivation and on performance.

Intrinsic and extrin- sic types of motivation have different effects on learning and performance, and the distinction is important to understanding how to promote learning and performance in school and other educational settings.
intrinsic motivation is positively related to creativity, whereas extrinsic motivation is negatively related to creativity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the self and the development of motivation.
the development of intrinsic motivation, the motivation that is derived from within the individual and is directed toward the task at hand.
the effects of intrinsic versus extrinsic motivation on cognitive performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

intrinsic motivation is the motivation that is inherent in an individual to do something without any external reward, whereas extrinsic motivation is the motivation of doing something in order to receive an external reward.
extrinsic motivation is not a single construct but a heterogeneous one that includes both controlled and autonomous forms.
intrinsic and extrinsic motivations are not two different things, but two different aspects of the same thing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
intrinsic motivation is the most important factor for a successful learning process and extrinsic motivation has to be seen as a means of supporting the intrinsic motivation.
intrinsic motivation reflects a natural human propensity to explore and assimilate information.
we are interested in how people learn and change.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the classic distinction between intrinsic and extrinsic types motivation is too simple.
extrinsic motivation, when it is not experienced as controlling, is a powerful source of self regulation that can be harnessed to promote learning and development in a wide variety of contexts.
intrinsic motivation is a very powerful and important construct, and that extrinsic motivation is more varied and complex than is often appreciated.
